public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-! # Woodall Primes

References:
* [Wikipedia/Woodall Number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodall_number#Woodall_primes)
* [A2234](https://oeis.org/A2234)

-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WoodallPrimes

/-- There are infinitely many prime numbers of the form `k * 2 ^ k - 1` for `k > 1`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem infinitely_many_woodall_primes : {k : ℕ | 1 < k ∧ (k * 2 ^ k - 1).Prime}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end WoodallPrimes

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of qualifying indices k > 1, whereas the source speaks of infinitely many distinct prime values of W_k = k·2^k − 1, with the Woodall sequence starting at k = 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: W_1 = 1 is not prime, so requiring k > 1 excludes no Woodall prime. Natural-number subtraction agrees with integer subtraction for every positive index. The map k ↦ k·2^k − 1 is strictly increasing, hence injective; its image on the qualifying indices is exactly the set of Woodall prime values. Infinitude of these two sets is therefore equivalent. This equivalence and the subtraction compatibility were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean without using the conjecture or sorry.

sources_consulted: OEIS A002234, read through its official data mirror: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A002/A002234.seq
review.notes: Checked the file’s sole declaration and the relevant Mathlib definitions. Lean computations for k = 0 through 10 match the sources, including primes 7, 23, and 383 at indices 2, 3, and 6. The research open tag agrees with Wikipedia; PrimePages explicitly states the infinitude conjecture. Direct OEIS requests were blocked by Cloudflare, so its complete sequence entry was read from the official data mirror. The final scratch file compiled successfully, and the equivalence proof has no sorryAx dependency.
